place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房后面 · 泥地里
place.en: Chending Temple · Behind the woodshed · in the mud

setup.zh: 那天辰时，小满没去讲堂。他蹲在柴房里，面前摆着那只小铜炉，跟它说话：「你叫什么？」
setup.en: That day, at the hour of the Dragon, Xiaoman didn't go to the lecture hall. He squatted in the woodshed with the little bronze burner in front of him and talked to it. "What's your name?" The lid didn't move.

recap.zh: 孙二狗架着你去了饭堂；阿禾问「谁打的？」；娘捎来一封信。你蹲在柴房里，问那只小铜炉叫什么。
recap.en: Sun Ergou held you up on the way to the dining hall; Ahe asked "Who did this?"; a letter came from your mother. You crouched in the woodshed and asked the little bronze furnace its name.

zh: 天快亮的时候，小路上有脚步声，一步一停。
小满把那封信看了三遍，揣进了怀里，贴着木牌。
en: Near dawn there were footsteps on the path, one step, a stop.
Xiaoman read the letter three times and tucked it into his coat, against the wooden tablet.
"…What's your name?" The lid does not stir.

label.en: The little beast on the lid

text.zh: 小兽闭着眼，只在你肚子咕咕叫的时候，才睁一睁。
text.en: The little beast keeps its eyes shut — it opens them only when your stomach growls.

text.zh: 山，水，一条弯弯的河，河边一座方方的城。你一拃拃不满它半圈。
text.en: Mountains, water, a winding river, and by it a square-walled town. Your hand's span won't reach halfway round.

story.zh:
天快亮的时候，小路上有脚步声，一步一停。是孙二狗，手里攥着一块井水浸过的布。孙二狗的铺挨着通铺那扇小窗，柴房后面那块空地，从那扇窗看出去，看得一清二楚。他蹲下，把那块布按在小满肿起来的左眼上，半天，才小声道：「……我没出来。」小满道：「我知道。」孙二狗道：「我怕。」小满道：「我也怕。怕，又不丢人。」孙二狗低着头，两只耳朵慢慢地红了，道：「等我……站得稳了。」后半句，他没说出来。

十月十三，小满让孙二狗架着，去了饭堂。他想，不去，就更像有事了。满饭堂的人偷偷地看他，看完了又偷偷地看马小宝。谁都知道是怎么回事。谁也没有说。马小宝端着空碗从他桌边经过，拿指头在他肩膀上戳了一戳，正戳在第二十三下那个地方：「师弟，摔得不轻啊。好好躺着，药园那头，有师兄呢。」

阿禾从山上下来了——她卯时进药园，在巡夜簿上看见了十二夜那一格。她端着碗在他对面坐下，先看他的脸，从左眼看到嘴角，道：「谁打的？」小满道：「摔的。」阿禾在本子上记了一笔，拿手挡着，他还是瞥见了一个圈。阿禾道：「你衣裳上的泥印子。一个印子一下。我数的。二十三。」小满吃了一惊。她从碗底下摸出一个煮鸡蛋，还是温的，放在他面前：「趁热吃了。」小满道：「……记账？」阿禾拿起炭条，落到纸上，停了很久，炭条的尖儿在纸上压出一个小黑点，慢慢洇开了一圈。后来她记了一笔，合上本子，道：「利息，这回……先不算。」端起碗走了，一次也没回头。

出了饭堂，药房门口停着济世堂送药材的挑子，挑子后头跟着一个光着两只脚的跑腿孩子。小满认出来了：廊下喊「那我就当那一个」的，就是他。那孩子从怀里掏出一封信来，信封上是舅舅的字：外甥沈小满亲启。

信不长。家里都好，勿念。娘的眼睛，夜里做针线熬坏了一点，不打紧。埋石蛋那夜，是这孩子帮我挖的坑。末了一行，字写得小了：**你爹如今天天进黑松岭。马家的狗不过断碑，他过。膝盖比去年重了，阴天下不了炕，晴天照去。我劝不住。**

小满把那封信看了三遍，揣进了怀里，贴着木牌。

那天辰时，小满没去讲堂。他蹲在柴房里，面前摆着那只小铜炉，跟它说话：「你叫什么？」炉盖一动不动。
story.en:
Near dawn there were footsteps on the path, one step, a stop. It was Sun Ergou, holding a cloth soaked in well water. Sun Ergou's place on the long bed was by the little window, and from that window you could see the open ground behind the woodshed as clear as day. He crouched down and pressed the cloth to Xiaoman's swollen left eye, and after a long while said quietly, "...I didn't come out." Xiaoman said, "I know." Sun Ergou said, "I was scared." Xiaoman said, "So was I. Being scared's nothing to be ashamed of." Sun Ergou kept his head down, and his ears slowly went red. He said, "When I'm... steady enough." The second half, he didn't say.

On the thirteenth of the tenth month Xiaoman went to the dining hall propped up by Sun Ergou. He thought: if I don't go, it'll look even more like something's happened. The whole dining hall stole looks at him, and when they'd looked, stole looks at Ma Xiaobao. Everybody knew what had happened. Nobody said a thing. Ma Xiaobao passed his table with an empty bowl and poked him in the shoulder with a finger, right on the spot where the twenty-third had landed. "Junior brother, that was a nasty fall. You lie down and rest. Your senior brother will see to the herb garden."

Ahe came down from the mountain. She had gone into the herb garden at the hour of the Rabbit and seen the square for the twelfth night in the night-watch book. She sat down opposite him with her bowl and looked at his face first, from his left eye to the corner of his mouth, and said, "Who hit you?" Xiaoman said, "I fell." Ahe made a note in her notebook, shielding it with her hand, but he still glimpsed a circle. Ahe said, "The mud marks on your clothes. One mark, one blow. I counted. Twenty-three." Xiaoman was startled. She took a boiled egg from under her bowl, still warm, and put it in front of him. "Eat it while it's warm." Xiaoman said, "...Going in the accounts?" Ahe picked up her charcoal and set it to the paper, and it stayed there a long time; the tip of the charcoal pressed a little black dot into the paper that slowly spread into a ring. Then she wrote something, closed the notebook, and said, "The interest, this time... I won't count it yet." She picked up her bowl and left, and never once looked back.

Outside the dining hall, at the door of the dispensary, stood the Jishi Hall's carrying pole with its load of medicinal herbs, and behind it a barefoot errand boy. Xiaoman recognised him: the one under the eaves who had shouted "Then I'll be the one!" The boy took a letter out of his coat. On the envelope was his uncle's hand: For my nephew Shen Xiaoman, to be opened by him.

The letter wasn't long. All well at home, don't worry. Your ma's eyes have been strained a little by sewing at night, nothing serious. The night we buried Shidan, it was this boy who helped me dig. The last line was written smaller: **Your pa goes into Black Pine Ridge every day now. The Ma dogs don't go past the broken stone; he does. His knees are worse than last year. On grey days he can't get off the kang; on clear days he goes all the same. I can't talk him out of it.**

Xiaoman read the letter three times and tucked it into his coat, against the wooden tablet.

That day, at the hour of the Dragon, Xiaoman didn't go to the lecture hall. He squatted in the woodshed with the little bronze burner in front of him and talked to it. "What's your name?" The lid didn't move.

exits.means: names the furnace 镇天神炉 — the lid ignores it

snub.zh: 炉盖纹丝不动。小兽睁开一只眼睛，瞥了你一眼，又闭上了。
snub.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast opens one eye, glances at you, and shuts it again.

exits.means: names the furnace 九转金丹炉 — the lid ignores it

snub.zh: 仍是不动。小兽翻了个身，拿屁股对着你。
snub.en: Still nothing. The little beast rolls over and turns its backside to you.

label.en: One Furnace of Heaven and Earth

exits.means: names the furnace 乾坤一炉 — the lid ignores it

snub.zh: 炉盖纹丝不动。小兽打了个大大的哈欠，连眼皮都懒得抬。
snub.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast gives a huge yawn, too lazy even to lift an eyelid.

exits.means: names the furnace 饭桶 (rice bucket) — the only name it takes; takes the furnace, keeps it

story.zh:
他一口气报了七八个镇上说书先生嘴里的名号，「镇天神炉」「九转金丹炉」「乾坤一炉」，越报越长，越报越响，它连动都懒得动。他从昨儿夜里到这会儿，只喝了一碗粥、吃了一个鸡蛋，肚子咕咕地叫，终于骂了一声：「你这饭桶，倒比我还难伺候。」只听「咔哒」一声，炉盖轻轻一跳，那小兽睁开一只眼睛，冲他眨了一眨——它看上的，偏偏是「饭桶」两个字。

它肚子上刻着一圈画，细得要眯起眼睛看：山，水，一条弯弯的河，河边一座方方的城。他拿拇指一拃，拃不满它半圈。可昨夜揣了一路，今早再托起来，他总觉得它比昨夜沉了一点。
story.en:
He reeled off seven or eight titles out of the mouths of the storytellers in town, "Heaven-Quelling Divine Burner", "Nine-Turn Golden Pill Burner", "The One Burner of Heaven and Earth", longer and longer, louder and louder, and it couldn't even be bothered to stir. Since last night he'd had only a bowl of porridge and an egg, his stomach was rumbling, and in the end he swore at it: "You rice bucket, you're harder to please than I am." There was a click, the lid gave a little jump, and the small beast opened one eye and winked at him. What it had taken a fancy to was, of all things, "rice bucket".

Round its belly was carved a ring of pictures, so fine you had to squint: mountains, water, a winding river, and by the river a square city. He spanned it with his thumb and fingers and couldn't cover half its girth. But having carried it all the way last night and lifting it again this morning, he couldn't help feeling it was a little heavier than last night.

refuse.zh: 炉盖纹丝不动。炉盖上的小兽打了个哈欠。
refuse.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast on the lid yawns.
